findings.text: Recognized assertion keys with vacuous values (tools_include:[] or result_contains:'') pass while still checking envelope framing and result-vs-error presence; this is a fixture-authoring quality concern, not a runner tautology (the no-rubber-stamp guard requires a recognized key, author-controlled).

summary: B18 (WARP-0318, MCP server/client runner) is correct and honest. Independent adversarial review: gate GREEN, both fixtures correct over the real stdio subprocess transport (pass exit 0; fail exit 1 naming the delete_everything bad tool call), four assertion-free/typo journeys all rejected as named journey errors (no rubber-stamp), capabilities mechanical honest (real transport runs in the gate), generic, ASCII, stdlib-only, both capabilities.yaml copies byte-identical. The review found one uncaught mutation (5/6): dropping the got-error-when-result-expected guard survived because the covering assertion used result_text. Post-review closure applied before ship and self-verified non-tautological: added two selftest assertions isolating that guard (an is_error:false and an empty result_contains expectation against a JSON-RPC error response), confirmed they FAIL when the guard is dropped and pass with it present, raising mutation coverage to 6/6. proof_digest recomputed via validate.py.
